Summary:
Security scan of secscan.us identified 3 security findings, none of them critical or high, yielding an overall grade of A with a risk score of 1/100.

Top priorities:
1. In your header config (middleware, next.config.js headers(), or Cloudflare/Railway rules), drop 'unsafe-inline' from style-src and set style-src 'self'.

Fix prompt (written for this codebase's AI editor — act on it directly):
I ran an automated security scan on secscan.us and found the following security issues that need to be fixed in my codebase.

### 1. Content-Security-Policy Allows Inline Styles (LOW)
My Content-Security-Policy sets style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', which permits injected CSS (script-src is fine and already has no unsafe-inline).
Fix: In whatever sets your response headers (framework middleware, next.config.js headers(), server or Cloudflare/Railway header rules), remove 'unsafe-inline' from style-src and set style-src 'self'. If inline styles must remain, use a nonce or hash instead. Tailwind compiles all styles to an external stylesheet in production, so first remove any remaining inline style= attributes in your markup, then drop unsafe-inline. Leave script-src 'self' as it is.

### 2. DNSSEC Not Enabled (INFO)
No DNSKEY records exist for secscan.us, so DNS answers could be forged in transit. This is not a code change: enable DNSSEC at your domain registrar and make sure your DNS host serves signed zones.

### 3. Active Security Testing Was Skipped (INFO)
Only passive checks ran; injection, XSS, path traversal, access control, SSRF and exposed backend data were not tested because this domain is not verified for the scanning account. This is not a code change: add the DNS TXT record or publish the verification file shown on your dashboard, then re-run the scan.

Please fix all of the above issues in my codebase. For each fix, show me the exact code change.

Findings 1–3 of 3, most severe first:

[LOW] Content-Security-Policy Allows Inline Styles (unsafe-inline in style-src) (CWE-79)
What: The Content-Security-Policy permits 'unsafe-inline' in style-src. Script execution is properly restricted (script-src has no unsafe-inline). CSS injection cannot execute JavaScript but can enable visual spoofing, clickjacking, and CSS-based data exfiltration via attribute selectors.
Fix: For the strongest defence, replace style-src 'unsafe-inline' with nonce-based or hash-based directives. For Tailwind CSS builds, all styles compile to an external stylesheet in production — unsafe-inline can usually be removed once any remaining inline style= attributes are eliminated.
Evidence: GET https://secscan.us/
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data:; img-src 'self' data: https: blob:; connect-src 'self' https: wss: ws:; worker-src 'self' blob:; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'
…

[INFO] DNSSEC Not Enabled (CWE-345)
What: DNSSEC is not configured for secscan.us. Without DNSSEC, DNS responses can be forged or tampered with in transit (DNS cache poisoning / Kaminsky attack). Attackers can redirect your domain's traffic to malicious servers without users or servers being able to detect it.
Fix: Enable DNSSEC through your domain registrar. Most major registrars (Cloudflare, AWS Route 53, Google Domains) offer one-click DNSSEC. Your DNS hosting provider must also support signed zones. This requires coordination between your registrar and DNS provider.
Evidence: No DNSKEY records found for secscan.us (NOERROR (name exists)).

[INFO] Active security testing was skipped for this scan
What: This scan checked only what an ordinary visitor can observe: response headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, exposed files and known-vulnerable versions. The checks that actively test for flaws — SQL injection, cross-site scripting, path traversal, broken access control, SSRF, and exposed Supabase/Firebase data — were not run, because they send real attack traffic and we only do that against a domain whose owner has asked us to. A clean result here does not mean those flaws are absent; it means they were not looked for.
Fix: Verify that you control this domain — add the DNS TXT record or publish the verification file shown on your dashboard — then run the scan again to include active testing.
Evidence: No verified ownership on record for this domain at scan time.

Compliance mapping note: This mapping shows which controls these findings are evidence for. It is not a compliance assessment, an audit, or an attestation. An application scan observes the HTTP surface of a running system at one point in time; SOC 2, PCI DSS and ISO 27001 are largely concerned with policy, process and personnel that no scan can see. A clean scan is not a passed control. Only a licensed CPA firm issues a SOC 2 report, only a QSA validates PCI DSS, and only an accredited certification body certifies ISO 27001.
